title: Ibuprofen-like activity in extra-virgin olive oil
authors: Beauchamp GK, Keast RS, Morel D, Lin J, Pika J, Han Q, et al.
funder: Funding statement not read: the main text is behind the publisher's paywall, and the archived article page and the supplementary methods contain no funding statement. Crossref metadata list no funder.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing financial interests.
result: Abstract: oleocanthal, a compound of newly pressed extra virgin olive oil whose pungency causes a stinging sensation in the throat, inhibits the same cyclooxygenase enzymes of the prostaglandin-biosynthesis pathway as ibuprofen, with a potency and profile the authors describe as strikingly similar. Supplementary methods: the irritant isolated from olive oil was identified by NMR as 2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)ethyl 4-formyl-3-(2-oxoethyl)-4-hexenoate, the deacetoxy-dialdehydic ligstroside aglycone; in commercial kit assays, (-)-oleocanthal inhibited ovine COX-1 and human recombinant COX-2 dose-dependently with IC50 values of 23 and 28 µM and did not affect soybean 15-lipoxygenase; the highest concentration among ten rated commercial oils was 200 µg/ml. The supplementary methods describe enzyme assays and sensory tests of throat irritation.
